{{Recipe summary
| Category = Fritter recipes
| Yield = 3 dozen
| Image = [[File:Koeksisters.JPG|300px]]
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of South Africa|Cuisine of South Africa]] | [[Cookbook:Confections|Confections]]

A '''koeksister''' is a fritter, usually in the shape of a plait, that is dipped in a cold syrup mixture. Koeksisters are very rich and are usually served as a special treat or kept for festive occasions. Making koeksisters is time-consuming and labour-intensive (another reason why it is not often made in modern day homes), so plan ahead to set a night and day aside for making this delicious treat. If you keep your oil hot and the syrup very cold you get the perfect koeksister—crisp and crunchy on the outside and soft, moist and syrupy on the inside. The syrup is made the night before to chill in the refrigerator in two containers. While making the koeksisters one of the containers is kept chilled in the refrigerator, to replace the other container of syrup when it heats up after a few batches of the fried dough have been dipped into the first container of syrup. If the syrup isn't cold, the dough won't soak up the syrup and you will end up with a dry koeksister.

== Ingredients ==

=== Syrup ===
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 500 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]) water
* 3 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] long piece of fresh [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], peeled and bruised '''OR''' 2–3 sticks of [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] (optional)
* 1 ml ([[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]]) [[Cookbook:Cream of Tartar|cream of tartar]]
* 1 pinch of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]]

=== Dough ===
* 240 g [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 4 tsp (20 ml) [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* 1 pinch of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] (30 ml) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 125 ml (½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]]) [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]] '''OR''' soured milk '''OR''' water mixed with [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] juice

== Procedure ==

=== Syrup ===
# Combine all ingredients in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], stirring until the sugar has dissolved.
# Turn the heat down, and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 5–8 minutes.
# Cool the [[Cookbook:Syrup|syrup]] to room temperature.
# Divide it into 2 containers, and place in the refrigerator to chill overnight.

=== Dough ===
# [[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] together flour, baking powder, and salt.
# Rub in butter.
# Add buttermilk. Mix into a soft [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] and [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] thoroughly. It helps if you oil your hands lightly when starting to knead the dough.
# Cover the dough with a damp cloth, and leave it to rest for 15 minutes.
# [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll]] the dough out to a thickness of 5 mm and cut into 5 x 70 mm (½ cm x 7 cm) strips. Press the ends of two or three strips together and twist or plait, then press the ends together again. Keep the dough you are not working with covered with a damp cloth.
# [[Cookbook:Deep fry|Deep fry]] in hot [[Cookbook:Oil_and_fat|oil]] until golden brown on both sides.
# Remove with a slotted spoon and dip the pieces immediately in the ice cold syrup.
# Remove and place the koeksisters on a wire rack so that the excess syrup can drain.
# Store the koeksisters in a sealed container in the refrigerator. They freeze well and can be served straight from the freezer.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* This recipe will yield about 3 dozen dainty-sized koeksisters—you can make them bigger for a more substantial treat.
* You may also, after dipping the fried koeksuster in the syrup, lightly roll it in dessicated coconut.
